c74object.name: bachmcp.database
c74object.digest: Analyse folders of sounds into a database, and query it
c74object.description: Builds a sound corpus: every sound in the folders and files given is analysed (librosa's and pyloudnorm's descriptors, ported to C++ with their defaults) and cut into units at five levels: the whole file; sections, where the material changes character; events, from one onset to the next; the attack, sustain and release phases of each event; and a fixed grid of slices. Each unit gets its own descriptors (loudness, spectral shape, MFCC, chroma, envelope, curves); each file gets CED's AudioSet tags (what it is: Drum, Speech, Bowed string instrument...), and a CLAP embedding, to find sounds like another one or like words. It all goes into one SQLite file, <package>/databases/<name>.db by default, which the algorithms query through this object (answered at once, as a dictionary) and the bach-mcp server and Python can read too. Analyses run on worker threads, never Max's; what they do is said in the Max console and out of the right outlet. Every sound is analysed at 48 kHz (its file is left as it is). The database remembers each file's size, date and content (a hash), so update analyses only what is new or has changed. Apple Silicon only. The models run through the core of bachmcp.onnxb~, which must sit next to this object (a model loads once, whichever object uses it), with ONNX Runtime in support/ (python py/main.py install) and the models downloaded (python py/main.py download ced-base, ... laion-clap-music-speech). Without a model the analysis goes on without its descriptors, says so, and leaves the sounds stale until reanalyse.

objarg.name: database
objarg.description: A name, for <package>/databases/<name>.db, or a path to a .db file. If it exists it is opened (read); otherwise build writes there.

inlet.digest: build, add, update, remove, read, write, query, sql, analysis...

outlet.digest: dictionary: answers (query, sql, info, files, analysis)
progress, done, open, written, closed, stale, error

method.name: build
method.digest: Make a new database from folders and files
method.description: Makes a new database and analyses every sound in these folders (their subfolders too with recursive 1) and files, with the object's analysis settings. Paths: full (/Users/me/sounds), ~/sounds, or as Max says them ("Macintosh HD:/Users/me/sounds"); quote a path with spaces. It writes to the box's database, or to @path <file> at the end of the message (build ~/sounds/drums @path ~/drums.db), or else to databases/<first folder's name>.db. A database already there is replaced. The folders and files become the database's sources, which update looks at again.

method.name: add
method.description: Adds these folders (with recursive as it is now) and files to the open database's sources, and analyses their sounds not in it yet. Brings back a path taken out with remove.

method.name: update
method.description: Looks at every source again (or those at or under the paths given), each searched as it was when added. A new sound is analysed (version 1). A sound whose size and date are the same is left alone, without being read. One whose size or date changed is hashed: if its content is the same, only its date is updated (touched); otherwise it is analysed again and its version goes up (changed). A sound that has gone, whose content turns up under a new path, was moved: its path is updated and its analysis kept. Otherwise it is marked missing and kept, or removed with prune 1. A file that can't be read as sound is kept as failed, with why, and tried again only once it changes.

method.name: remove
method.description: Takes the sounds at or under these paths out of the database, with their units, and the sources at or under them. A path inside a source that stays is remembered, so update doesn't bring it back; add it to bring it back.

method.name: reanalyse
method.description: reanalyse or reanalyse stale: analyses again the sounds made with other settings (see analysis) or an older version of the object. reanalyse all: every sound. Paths after it limit it to the sounds at or under them. Their units are replaced, so their ids change and their versions go up.

method.name: analysis
method.digest: Set or show the analysis settings
method.description: Alone: sends the settings out of the left outlet, as a dictionary (of says whose: database when one is open, else object). With keys and values (analysis grid_ms 200 hpss 0; analysis levels section event): changes them. They are the object's, which build uses, and an open database's too: a database keeps its settings, and add, update and reanalyse always use them. When an open database's settings change, its sounds become stale (the right outlet says stale <n>) until reanalyse. The keys are in the discussion below.

method.name: read
method.description: Opens a database: a name in databases/, or a path. Alone: the box's. Its settings become the object's. The right outlet says open <path>.

method.name: write
method.description: Writes a copy of the open database (a name in databases/, or a path), safely while it is open. The object goes on with the one it has open: a database is saved as it changes, so write is only for a copy.

method.name: compact
method.description: Rebuilds the database file to give back the space left by removed and reanalysed sounds (SQLite reuses it but never returns it). It takes a while on a big database, and queries wait for it. The right outlet then says compacted <bytes before> <bytes after>.

method.name: close
method.description: Closes the open database. The right outlet says closed.

method.name: cancel
method.description: Stops the build, add, update or reanalyse running, after the sounds being analysed now (they are kept), and drops the jobs waiting after it. What was done stays done; update later finishes the rest.

method.name: query
method.description: Answers at once, out of the left outlet, with the units that match (see the discussion). The query: the name of a dictionary (query mydict), words in dictionary syntax (query level: event where: { envelope: impulse } order: -peak_db limit: 5) or JSON. It reads beside a running job, so an algorithm can query while the database grows. near: { text: "a bowed string" } searches by words; the first such query loads the CLAP if no job has (a second or two).

method.name: dictionary
method.description: The same as query <name>: a dictionary sent to the object is a query.

method.name: sql
method.description: Runs one SQL statement that only reads (SELECT ...) and answers at once, out of the left outlet: columns, the column names; rows, one dictionary per row; count; truncated when more than 10000 rows. Quote the statement in a message box, where a comma would end the message: sql "SELECT level, count(*) AS n FROM units GROUP BY level". The tables are in the discussion.

method.name: info
method.description: Sends a dictionary out of the left outlet: path, bytes on disk, files and their states, stale, duration_ms (of the sounds), units and their levels, sources, excluded, settings, core (the version that analysed them), created.

method.name: files
method.description: Sends a dictionary out of the left outlet whose items are the database's sounds: id, path, state (ok, missing, failed), version, stale, units, duration_ms, rate and channels (the file's own), analysed (date), error.

attribute.name: recursive
attribute.description: 1 (default): build and add search a folder's subfolders too. 0: only the sounds directly in it. Each source keeps the way it was added: changing this later changes only the next build or add. Hidden files and folders (starting with a dot) are always left out.

attribute.name: threads
attribute.description: How many sounds are analysed at the same time. Each analysis holds about 100 MB per minute of sound: with long sounds (an hour is about 6 GB), lower it.

attribute.name: prune
attribute.digest: update removes sounds gone from disk
attribute.description: 0 (default): a sound gone from disk is marked missing and kept, with its analysis (it comes back if the file does). 1: update removes it.

attribute.name: label
attribute.value: update removes sounds gone from disk

attribute.name: verbose
attribute.description: What a job says in the Max console. 0: when it starts and its summary at the end. 1 (default): also one line per sound that was analysed, changed, moved, missing or removed (its version, duration, units and the seconds it took). 2: every sound, unchanged ones too. A sound that fails is always said, as an error.

attribute.name: label
attribute.value: Console: 0 start and end, 1 changes, 2 every file

c74object.discussion:
The right outlet progress <index> <total> <status> <path>, for each sound a job looks at (status: analysed, changed, reanalysed, unchanged, touched, moved, missing, removed, failed); done <analysed> <changed> <moved> <missing> <removed> <failed> <seconds> at the end of a job; open <path>; written <path>; closed; stale <n> after new settings; compacted <bytes before> <bytes after>; error <words> (also in the console).
Queries Every key is optional. level: file, section, event, phase, grid, or a list of them (default: all). where: a dictionary of conditions, all of which must hold: a number or a word, equal (envelope: impulse); [ min max ], a range, null for no bound (centroid_mean: [ 2000 null ]); a list of words, one of them (phase: [ attack release ]); also path (the file's path contains it), name (the file's name), and tags, a label or a list of them, any of a file's best labels (tags: Speech; tag is only the best one). near: { unit: 412 by: [ mfcc_mean centroid_mean ] } finds the units most like unit 412 by these descriptors (default mfcc_mean), or { centroid_mean: 1500 lufs: -20 } the units nearest these values, or { text: "a drum loop" } the units whose CLAP embedding is nearest these words (by: [ clap ] compares units by their embeddings); each descriptor is standardized over the candidates (each dimension of a list), so descriptors in different units weigh the same, and each unit gets its distance; clap is compared by angle (1 - cosine), and each unit also gets its similarity, the cosine (with text alone, distance is 1 - similarity). order: a descriptor, rising, -descriptor falling, or random; with near, by distance. limit: how many (default 20). fields: the keys each unit comes with, or all; default: id, file, path, level, parent, start_ms, end_ms, duration_ms, the labels, and the descriptors the query names. The answer: count, matched (before limit), units.
A unit id; file; level; parent (the unit it is part of: a section's file, an event's section, a phase's event; a grid slice's file); start_ms, end_ms in its file. Descriptors, each unit over its own span: duration_ms, peak_db, rms_db, lufs and lra (from 400 ms on), temporal_centroid_ms, harmonic_share, onset_count, onset_density, ioi_mean_ms, ioi_cv; for level, centroid, bandwidth, rolloff, flatness, zcr and flux: _mean, _std, _p10, _p90, _slope (centroid_mean...). Lists: mfcc_mean, mfcc_std, mfcc_delta_mean, mfcc_delta_std, mfcc_delta2_mean, mfcc_delta2_std (13 each), chroma_mean (12, C to B), level_curve, centroid_curve, flux_curve (20 points). A file: tuning (semitones); tag, its best AudioSet label, and tag_score (0-1); tags, its tag_count best labels, a list of { label, score }; tag_scores, the score of every one of the 527 labels, in CED's order. A file (and the units of the other levels in clap_levels, at least clap_min_ms long): clap, the unit embedding (512 numbers for LAION CLAP). A section: form (A, B, ... the same letter for similar sections), novelty, repeats, repeat_similarity. An event: envelope (impulse, sustained, iterative), has_attack, attack_ms, log_attack, sustain_ms, release_ms, reattacks. A phase: phase (attack, sustain, release).
Analysis settings rate (48000; 0: each file's own), n_fft (2048), hop (512), n_mels (128), n_mfcc (20), roll_percent (0.85), hpss (1; 0 is faster, without harmonic_share), hpss_kernel (31), chroma (1), levels (file section event phase grid), novelty_ms (4000: the scale of the sections), novelty_threshold (0.1), snap_ms (500), repeat_similarity (0.8), silence_db (-60), min_event_ms (50), sustain_db (6), decay_db_per_s (24), min_sustain_ms (100), grid_ms (100), grid_hop_ms (100: no overlap; grid slices quieter than silence_db are left out), light_levels (phase grid: these levels' units get only the means, mfcc_mean and chroma_mean, no std, p10, p90, slope, MFCC std or deltas, curves; they are many and short, and this keeps a database about a quarter of its full size; none for every level in full), curve_points (20), extensions (wav wave aif aiff aifc flac mp3 m4a caf). The models, by their names in models/catalog.toml, or none: tagger (ced-base; ced-mini is faster), tag_count (10), tag_threshold (0.05), clap (laion-clap-music-speech, as the MCP; laion-clap2-m and laion-clap2-l are much better at speech and music), clap_levels (file; add section, event... for embeddings of their units, at a cost in time), clap_min_ms (250), windows (3: a sound longer than the model hears at once is heard in up to this many windows, as the MCP hears it). The models are most of the time a build takes: analysis tagger none clap none for a quick one.
The tables (for sql) units: one row per unit, one column per descriptor (lists are stored as 16-bit floats, numpy.frombuffer(blob, "<f2") in Python, and come back as lists; values in Hz and ms are whole numbers). files: id, path, name, size, mtime, hash, version, settings_id, core, state, rate, channels, duration_ms, analysed, error. sources: path, folder, recursive. excluded: path. meta: key, value (the settings, as JSON). Join a unit to its file with units.file = files.id.
